newsitem.title: USA: Stocks and bonds end lower ahead of price data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks and bonds end lower ahead of price data.

text.p: Stocks edged lower and bond prices fell for the fourth straight session Thursday as investors awaited Friday's wholesale price and retail sales reports for September.
Copper prices rose to their highest level in five weeks on worries about tight supplies. The dollar edged lower and crude oil fell.

The Dow Jones industrial average fell 8.95 points to 5,921.67. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,244 to 1,080 on subdued volume of 394 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Friday's data on producer prices and the pace of retail sales could give the market a scare if they show signs of inflationary pressures, analysts said.
"Friday's session is likely to show a reaction to the Federal Reserve's interest-rate perspective," said Alan Ackerman, senior market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.

Last month, the Fed held interest rates unchanged, but some on Wall Street were betting that the central bank might have been waiting for additional economic data before making up its mind on whether or not to raise short-term rates.

The stock market jumped last Friday on an unexpectedly weak employment report for September but has since backtracked, with the Dow Jones index unable to retain rallies through the 6,000-point milestone.

Adding to nervousness are third-quarter earnings reports, which are due to begin in earnest next week, with companies including Johnson & Johnson, Coca-Cola Co., Citicorp and Time Warner Inc. due to post their results.
Wall Street bears, a dwindling breed, are saying that the Dow's inability to close above 6,000 barrier is a sign that stocks are losing momentum.
"Earnings could be a critical factor here in pushing the market over," said James Solloway, director of Research at Argus Research Corp.
But bulls said they saw no major danger on the horizon.

"We don't see much in the way of downside here at all," said Ken Tower, technical analyst at UST Securities. He cited the recent drop in the long-term interest rate below 7 percent, and the likelihood it will stabilise at that level.
Bond prices fell on renewed inflation worries, the fourth straight declining session.
The bellwether 30-year Treasury dropped 22/32, or $6.875 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.89 percent from 6.83 percent on Wednesday.
Investors said bearish comments by a top Fed official combined with a surprising drop in jobless claims reignited inflation jitters.
In currency markets, the dollar traded in a tight range and edged lower against major currencies.
The dollar pierced the important 1.53 German mark level but fell back to end at 1.5282, compared with 1.5284 at Wednesday's close.
With Japanese trading floors shut due to a national holiday, the dollar drifted lower against the yen to end at 111.18 yen, below Wendesday's 111.53 close.
Crude oil fell 81 cents to $24.26 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Copper prices reached a five-week high Thursday ahead of a report Friday that is expected to confirm that global supplies are dwindling.
Copper for December delivery jumped 1.90 cents to 92.25 cents a pound at New York's Commodity Exchange.
Overseas, stocks in London fell, with the FTSE 100 index off 14.6 points to end at 3,994.7. The Tokyo stock market was closed for a national holiday and will reopen on Friday.
